newsitem.title: USA: Germany's Neuer Markt sees 20 stocks by year's end.
newsitem.headline: Germany's Neuer Markt sees 20 stocks by year's end.

text.p: Germany's Neuer Markt exchange, designed to attract smaller high-growth companies, could more than double its listings to about 20 stocks by the end of the year, a German stock exchange official said Monday.

Gunter Femers, a senior vice president of the Deutsche Borse and one of the four-month-old exchange's organizers, told reporters additions to the seven shares on the exchange would largely come through initial public offerings (IPOs) instead of secondary listings from other stocks.
"There's a chance for double listings but its only a handful," he said. "The majority of the 20-plus companies ... will be IPOs."
The Frankfurt exchange added document management company SER Systeme AG and custom tool developer Saltus Technology AG Monday. SER closed at 105 marks and Saltus at 59.50 marks.

Femers, who spoke at a news conference on the exchange, said the Neuer Markt was designed to attract small- and medium-capitalization companies with high growth potential, similar to the United States' Nasdaq exchange.
Neuer Markt is German for "new market." It is part of the Deutsche Borse AG and a companion to the much larger Frankfurt stock exchange.

Companies that list on the Neuer Markt exchange gain a higher profile with potential investors, Femers and other officials said. However, in exchange they must meet standards of greater transparency than other German stocks.

Among them are bookkeeping under International Accounting Standards or U.S. Generally Accepted Accounting Principles, publication of share ownership of senior management, seminars for equity analysts and release of schedules for company announcements.

"The main attraction for anybody joining the Neuer Markt is that they are on an elevated platform," Femers said. "We ... demand quite a bit of transparency and publicity from them to make them more attractive."
The average daily volume is $30 million and the Neuer Markt has 23 so-called "market makers" such as banks and brokers that guarantee the exchange's liquidity.
